title: Ideas worth keeping
text: A useful page has a rhythm: a thought, an example, a pause. Emphasis gives one phrase its place, and strong text makes a point easy to find again. A notebook is a place to think on paper, and a place to return to that thought. title: The shape of a page
text: The first obligation of a page is to be read. A comfortable line, a generous margin, and an unhurried rhythm do much of the work. Consistency makes the details useful: the space above a heading, the weight of a rule, the way a link sits inside a sentence. This paragraph contains emphasis, a stronger point, and an ordinary link. An expression such as library.find() has a different voice. Numbers 0123456789, “quotation marks,” and an em dash — all belong to the same typographic system.

title: The shape of a page
text: A heading helps the reader skim and settle back into the text. Start with a concrete question or a small example. Explain enough for the reader to understand the decision. Leave a useful route to the next idea. Read a little, think a little, and keep something worth returning to. A quieter detail can sit in its own place without interrupting the argument. This note folds away until the reader needs the detail.
